mrv_findings.text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — [P1, confidence 100] `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` chooses one of multiple permitted rows for the same case-insensitive host because neither the model nor schema enforces host uniqueness, so adding a second category mapping silently leaves imports routed to the first mapping instead of the newly configured category.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:5 — [P2, confidence 100] `t.integer :category_id, null: false` has no foreign key and the model only declares `belongs_to :category`, so the controller can persist a nonexistent category ID and subsequently pass that dangling ID to topic creation as a supposedly valid host/category relationship.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — [P2 confidence=100] The validator fragment `[a-z]{2,5}` rejects valid hosts such as `example.museum` and `example.technology`, preventing administrators from creating or editing category relationships for these domains.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:6 — [P2 confidence=100] `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` dereferences nil before validation when an API create/update omits or nulls the host, returning an unhandled server error instead of the intended validation response.

app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:16 — [P2 confidence=100] `host.destroy` is unconditional after a nullable lookup, so deleting a host already removed by another administrator raises NoMethodError instead of handling the stale-record edge case, and update similarly passes nil into `save_host(host)`.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — [confidence 100, P1] `WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i` indexes an empty result when embedding is unconfigured or the configured category no longer exists, aborting migration before the intended uncategorized fallback and blocking upgrades for those databases.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — [confidence 100, P1] `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"` copies previously accepted URL-form hosts verbatim without the new model's normalization, so an existing value such as `https://example.com/1234` can never match the new hostname-only lookup and embedding stops after upgrade.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31 — [confidence 100, P1] `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"` destroys the legacy settings inside `change` without an inverse or backup, making the data migration irreversible and leaving the previous application unable to recover its embedding configuration on rollback.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31 — [confidence 75, P1] `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"` removes the old readers' source of truth in the same migration that introduces its replacement, so old workers during a rolling deployment reject embedding after refreshing settings and their subsequent setting writes are never copied into the new table.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — [P2 confidence 75] `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"` interpolates persisted host-setting text without quoting or parameters, so a legacy value containing a quote can escape the SQL literal and execute injected SQL with migration privileges.

spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:6 — [P1 confidence 100] `expect(Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController).to eq(true)` only checks inheritance and never exercises create/update/destroy, so all new host/category persistence, default-category, and validation-error behavior can fail while this entire controller spec passes.

spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:6 — [P2 confidence 100] `expect(Admin::EmbeddingController < Admin::AdminController).to eq(true)` never requests show/update or inspects the serialized host/category relationships, so a broken embedding response that prevents the new editor from loading remains undetected by its new controller spec.
